entries.text: API · o-app and o-page o-app and o-page The app container manages the page stack and navigation; a page instance manages its own screen of content. o-app instance Member Description app.src URL of the app config module app.current Current page instance (read-only) app.routers Route history array, both readable and writable app.goto(src) Navigates and pushes onto the stack app.replace(src) Replaces the current page without pushing onto the stack app.back(delta = 1) Goes back app.forward(delta = 1) Goes forward (requires allowForward) app.appIsReady The first page has finished rendering (read-only) app._module App config: home, loading, fail, access, allowForward, pageAnime o-page instance Member Description page.src URL of the page module, immutable after initialization page.pageIsReady Flag indicating the page has finished rendering (read-only) page.goto(src) / page.replace(src) Resolves the URL against the current page, then navigates page.back() Goes back page.pageAnime Animation config for this page, readable and writable page._rendered Promise that resolves when the page finishes rendering ← Back to API overview

entries.title: Context Communication — ofa.js API
entries.description: o-provider puts data into a subtree and o-consumer consumes the nearest one; instance methods can also look up providers.
entries.text: API · Context communication Context communication o-provider puts data into a subtree and o-consumer consumes the nearest one; instance methods can look up a provider proactively. Members Member Description el.getProvider(name) Searches upward across shadow boundaries for an o-provider with the same name, falls back to o-root-provider, and returns null when neither exists provider.dispatch(name, { data }) Dispatches a custom event to that provider's consumers $.getRootProvider(name) Gets the app-level root provider instance Tip: a provider's HTML attribute is read only once, at initialization; to update it at runtime, change the provider's data property directly. ← Back to API overview

entries.title: Events — ofa.js API
entries.description: Bind, unbind, and dispatch events with instance methods; events can carry payload data and cross shadow boundaries.
entries.text: API · Events Events Bind, unbind, and dispatch events with instance methods; events can carry payload data and cross shadow boundaries. Members Member Description el.on(name, handler) Bind an event; returns el so calls can be chained el.one(name, handler) Fire once and unbind automatically el.off(name, handler) Unbind an event el.emit(name, opts) Dispatch an event; opts.data is attached as event.data and the remaining fields are passed as Event init options Tip: on:click="method" in a template is unbound automatically when the component unmounts, so there is no need to call off manually. ← Back to API overview

entries.title: Instance Basics — ofa.js API
entries.description: An instance is a DOM wrapper, reactive data, and a child-element collection all at once. Start with its basic properties.
entries.text: API · Instance basics Instance basics An instance object is a DOM wrapper, reactive data, and a collection of child elements all at once. Start by getting to know its basic properties. Members Member Description el.ele The native DOM element; every browser API is reached through it el.tag Lowercase tag name (read-only) el.owner The data ownership chain (a Set); reactive updates bubble up along it (read-only) el.length Number of child elements, matching ele.children.length (read-only) el[0], el[1] Read a child element instance by index (read-only) el.index Position within the parent; null when there is no parent (read-only) el.PATH Location of the component / page file; relative resources resolve against it (read-only) el.app Nearest o-app instance; undefined when outside an app (read-only) el.shadow The element's own shadow root instance (read-only) el.root The root node it lives in: document or some shadow root (read-only) el.host Nearest shadow host component instance (read-only) el.xid Unique identifier of the instance, used to tell apart instances with the same tag (read-only) Note: Members marked “read-only” are maintained internally by the instance; assigning to them does not change the structure. ← Back to API overview

entries.description: Read and write text, HTML, attributes, classes, and inline styles.
entries.text: API · Content, Attributes & Styles Content, Attributes & Styles Read and write text, HTML, attributes, classes, and inline styles. Members Member Description el.text Read and write textContent (reactive) el.html Read and write innerHTML (reactive) el.attr(name[, value]) Read or write an HTML attribute; relative href/src inside a component resolve against PATH automatically el.prop(name[, value]) Read or write a data property (same as el[name]); supports dot paths el.class(name[, bool]) Read / toggle a class el.classList Native DOMTokenList el.data Native dataset (not reactive) el.style Native inline style object (not reactive) el.css Style proxy: falls back to computed styles when there is no inline value; supports --variables el.refresh() Manually dispatch one refresh update event Tip: el.css can be written one property at a time (el.css.color), replaced wholesale as an object, or replaced wholesale as a string. ← Back to API overview

entries.title: Data & Watchers — ofa.js API
entries.description: Instance data comes from stanz: reading and writing fields is reactive, with dedicated methods for watching and cleanup.
entries.text: API · Data & Watchers Data & Watchers Instance data comes from stanz: reading and writing fields is a reactive update, and watching and cleanup each have dedicated methods. Members Member Description el.watch(cb) Watch changes on the instance and its children; returns a watcher id el.watchTick(cb) Same as watch, but a batch of changes in one tick fires only once el.unwatch(id) Unregister a watcher el.watchUntil(fn, timeout = 30000) A Promise that resolves once the condition holds and unbinds itself; the timeout defaults to 30 seconds el.refresh(opts) Manually dispatch a refresh event without changing data el.sync(prop, path, options) Two-way sync action; for template sync: only, and calling it directly throws el.toJSON() / el.toString() Export a plain object (recursive) / a JSON string el.revoke() Revoke the instance: clears watchers and drops data references Tip: watchUntil only evaluates on data changes and does not check immediately after registration; if the condition may already hold, check it yourself once first. ← Back to API overview

entries.title: Structure Operations — ofa.js API
entries.description: Operate on child elements with array semantics; mutating methods really move DOM nodes and trigger updates.
entries.text: API · Structure operations Structure operations Child elements work with array semantics; mutating methods really move DOM nodes and trigger updates. Members Member Description push(...items) Append child elements at the end; returns the new child element count unshift(...items) Insert child elements at the beginning; returns the new child element count pop() / shift() Remove the last / first child element and return its instance splice(start, count, ...items) Delete and insert; returns an array of the removed instances reverse() / sort(fn) Reverse / sort child elements in place map / filter / slice / forEach Non-mutating array methods: materialize an array of instances first, then run el.before(content) / el.after(content) Insert content before / after the element itself el.remove() Remove the element from its parent (through splice, so event semantics are intact) el.wrap(content) Wrap the element with content; throws when there is no parent el.unwrap() Remove the element's own wrapper; throws when there is more than one sibling el.clone(bool = true) Clone the element, including child elements by default Tip: Manipulating child elements directly does not update the array in data; use o-fill for template lists. ← Back to API overview

entries.title: Selection & Traversal — ofa.js API
entries.description: Find elements inside an instance and move across DOM and shadow boundaries.
entries.text: API · Selection and traversal Selection and traversal Find elements inside an instance and move back and forth across DOM and shadow boundaries. Members Member Description el.$(expr) Find the first match inside the instance; inside a component, use this.shadow.$() el.all(expr) Find every match inside the instance and return an array of instances el.parent The parent element instance; null when the parent is document el.parents Array of all ancestor instances el.parentsUntil(expr) Collect ancestors upward until expr is matched (that node excluded) el.hosts The chain of shadow hosts, level by level el.next / el.nexts The next sibling / all following sibling elements el.prev / el.prevs The previous sibling / all preceding sibling elements el.siblings All sibling elements except the element itself el.is(expr) Whether it matches a selector, or equals an instance or native element el.contains(expr) Whether it contains a given selector, instance, or native element el.composedPath() The event system's full path (across shadow boundaries), returned as an array of native nodes el.get("a.b.c") Read a value by dot path; a single key is the same as direct access el.set("a.b.c", value) Assign a value by dot path; a single key is the same as direct assignment Tip: In the example, second.prev / second.next are sibling instances; class() toggles class names on and off. ← Back to API overview

entries.title: How Much Better Is ofa.js v5 Than v4? — ofa.js
entries.description: A grounded look at what changed between ofa.js v4 and v5: architecture, rendering, list performance, routing, and developer experience.
headings: 2. List performance: this time it is measurable
3. From separate repositories to a monorepo: four packages, one repository
4. Templates and rendering: fixing the “works until it doesn't” edges
6. State and context: same API, tighter implementation
8. AI-assisted development with a shorter feedback loop
9. Migration cost: lower than expected, but not zero
entries.text: ← Back to blog Engineering · Version comparison How much better is ofa.js v5 than v4? v5 is not a release that merely adds APIs. It keeps the way you write ofa.js applications, but rebuilds template rendering, list reconciliation, module boundaries, and routing edge cases underneath. 2026-11-22 9 min read Based on ofa.js 5.0 and 4.7.7 o-if / o-fill LIS reconciliation monorepo AI-assisted The shortest accurate summary is: it still looks like ofa.js on the surface, but the runtime below has been rebuilt on cleaner foundations. The v4 ideas—components, pages, o-app , o-page , provider/consumer, zero-build—are still here. What changed is the machinery underneath them. 1. The short answer For most application code, migrating to v5 is not expensive: the template syntax is largely the same, pages and components are organized the same way, and SCSR real-path routing continues. But if you care about performance, maintainability, or template edge cases, the changes are substantial: List reconciliation uses LIS, making swaps, partial updates, and batch operations dramatically faster. The core moved from separate repositories into one monorepo: drill, stanz, xhear, and ofajs now evolve together. Template rendering uses the xhear v9 pipeline; o-if and o-fill moved down into xhear and were rewritten. The old x-* syntax is gone; o-* is the only template vocabulary. The app layer no longer depends on a global window.lm , and error codes moved into the framework. Routing handles leaving pages, nested layout reflows, and related edge cases more reliably. AI-assisted development is backed by shared tests, docs, and context in the same repository. 2. List performance: this time it is measurable The hardest improvement is in the list runtime. The old reconciliation had two structural problems: any deep item change could refresh the entire list, and index-based reconciliation with indexOf degraded to O(n²) on swaps while moving far more DOM nodes than necessary. v5 uses structural checks, LIS reconciliation, lightweight row contexts, binding-level dependency filtering, and batched undo. In the repository's benchmark—same machine, Chromium 156, median of three runs—the numbers moved like this: Scenario v4 (4.7.7) v5 (5.0) Swap two items in 1,000 rows 3020ms 120ms Ten partial updates 421ms 93ms Append 1,000 rows 247ms 39ms Delete 100 rows 53ms 20ms Clear 2,000 rows 35ms 16ms This is an internal benchmark, not a promise for every device or data shape. Building 1,000 rows and first paint improve much less (roughly 38ms → 34ms, with first paint around 69ms unchanged), because that cost is dominated by module execution and element registration, not list reconciliation. But for swaps, batch deletes, and partial updates—the operations that tend to hurt—the gap is no longer in the same range. On bundle size: v4's ofa.min.mjs is 75,749 B (25,327 B gzip, 22,662 B brotli); the v5 build is 69,914 B (24,168 B gzip, 21,552 B brotli). That is roughly 7.7% smaller raw, 4.6% smaller gzip, and 4.9% smaller brotli. It is not an order-of-magnitude change, but it does show the performance work did not come from piling on code. Why are swaps the biggest win? The old implementation recomputed key mappings after every move, so swapping two items cascaded into a series of DOM moves. The new implementation first uses LIS to find the smallest set of nodes that truly need to move, then commits the changes in a batch. 3. From separate repositories to a monorepo: four packages, one repository In the v4 era, the core capabilities were spread across separate repositories: drill loaded browser modules, stanz provided Proxy-based reactive data, xhear owned Web Components and template compilation, and ofajs added the application layer—pages, routing, context, and o-link . Each could work on its own, but cross-repository changes, integration testing, and version alignment were painful. The core change in v5 is not “splitting things up again.” It is bringing those previously separate repositories into one monorepo so they evolve together. The four packages still have clear boundaries, but a cross-package change can land in one commit and be verified by one test run and one build. Maintaining ofa.js itself also gets easier. In the multi-repository era, upgrading ofa.js often meant syncing versions, tests, and issues across repositories. Now a change and its downstream impact on drill, stanz, and xhear live in the same repository: searching, jumping to definitions, running tests, and debugging no longer require switching repos. A repro, a fix, and a regression test can land in one commit—updating ofa.js and tracking down problems both take a much shorter path. That matters for the framework itself: when the xhear rendering pipeline changes, the ofajs page/routing tests can run in the same pass; when stanz changes how reactive updates are emitted, it is immediately visible whether xhear list re-rendering regressed. ofajs also explicitly imports the loader it needs instead of relying on a global lm that happens to exist on the page. v5 also moved the error-code table into the framework and removed the separate ofa-error package. Another easy-to-miss change is the release shape: the source is the artifact . Apart from the main ofa.js package and a few bridge packages that use rollup, packages remain source-only ESM. The .mjs the browser executes is the source in the repository, so debugging does not bounce between a source map and the real implementation. 4. Templates and rendering: fixing the “works until it doesn't” edges v4's template system was already capable, but it sat on the older xtext / x-bind-data pipeline. After moving rendering to xhear v9, o-if and o-fill are no longer simple “wrap a template” directives. They compile on demand, cache the compiled result, and use a descriptor fast path. The practical result is that combinations which could silently fail in complex templates now behave predictably, for example: an o-fill inside an o-if ; an o-if inside each o-fill item; table rows rendered through replace-temp ; named templates that recursively reference themselves. v5 also explicitly removes x-if , x-else-if , x-else , and x-fill . Those elements are no longer registered; using them produces a deprecation message instead of quietly behaving differently. Template semantics and documentation now have one vocabulary: o-* . <!-- v4 --> <x-fill :value = "rows" ></x-fill> <!-- v5 --> <o-fill :value = "rows" ></o-fill> 5. Routing and pages: from “works” to “stable” v5 continues to use SCSR real paths: each URL maps to an HTML document, can be deployed to a static server, and can be adopted by o-app as a nested page. v4 proved the model; v5 fixes the edges: Leaving pages lock their size and position during layout changes instead of jumping to the top-left. Nested routes keep a shared parent via export const parent , so switching child pages does not rebuild the parent. waitPageReaded reuses the page's _rendered promise instead of polling. o-app supports access , allowForward , page animations, and a clear failure page. None of these is huge alone, but together they make page transitions feel more predictable. In particular, going from the home page into the docs and back no longer makes the old page flash while the layout reflows. 6. State and context: same API, tighter implementation o-provider , o-consumer , and o-root-provider remain, now explicitly walking composedPath across shadow boundaries. getProvider , watchUntil , and access keep the v4 feel. The difference is a more disciplined implementation: context data no longer relies on globals, components and pages know which app or provider they belong to, and the rule that an o-consumer 's light children are not compiled is covered by tests. In practice that means fewer “why didn't this update?” moments rather than a new learning curve. 7. Engineering and ecosystem: zero-build, still v4 made “no bundler” a defining feature, and v5 does not abandon it.

entries.title: o-app Applications — ofa.js Docs
entries.description: o-app configuration, page stack, transition animations, loading/fail states, and extending proto.
entries.text:
Application o-app Applications o-app is a micro-app container. It loads an application configuration module and manages the page stack, page transition animations, and navigation events, but it does not load page HTML itself. Minimal application // app-config.js export const home = "./pages/home.html"; The src of o-app must be an application configuration module; it cannot point directly to a page. To run a single page standalone, use . Application configuration export const home = "./pages/home.html"; export const pageAnime = { current: { opacity: 1, transform: "translate(0, 0)" }, next: { opacity: 0, transform: "translate(30px, 0)" }, previous: { opacity: 0, transform: "translate(-30px, 0)" }, }; export const loading = () => "
Loading...
"; export const fail = ({ src, error }) => `
Failed to load: ${src}
`; export const allowForward = true; // Cross-origin page access control: return true to allow, false or an Error to deny export const access = (src) => src.startsWith("https://cdn.example.com/"); export const proto = { goHome() { this.goto("home.html"); }, get isHome() { return this.current?.src.includes("home.html"); }, }; export const ready = function () { console.log("app is ready", this.current); }; Export Description home Home page address loaded at startup pageAnime Three-state page transition animation: current / next / previous loading HTML shown while a page is loading fail HTML shown when loading fails; receives { src, error } allowForward Whether forward() is allowed; off by default access Cross-origin page access control; return true to allow. Not needed for same-origin pages proto Methods and getters added to the o-app instance ready Callback after the configuration has loaded; this is the app instance access receives a page src and must return true for a cross-origin page to load; returning false or an Error rejects it. The target site must still configure CORS correctly, otherwise the browser blocks the request first. App instance const app = $("o-app"); app.current; // current page instance app.appIsReady; // first page has rendered (wait with watchUntil) app.routers; // routing stack; parent layout pages do not enter it app.goto("./pages/detail.html?id=1"); app.replace("./pages/detail.html"); app.back(); app.forward(); // requires allowForward: true Inside a page module you can also call this.goto , this.replace , and this.back directly; this.app points to the app the page belongs to. Watching routing changes const app = $("o-app"); app.on("router-change", (event) => { console.log(event.data.name); // goto / replace / back / forward console.log(event.data.src); // target page URL }); Page animations pageAnime.current is the state of a settled page, next is the entry start for the incoming page, and previous is the exit end for the outgoing page. All three states can be omitted; defaults are used when they are. export const pageAnime = { current: { opacity: 1, transform: "translateX(0)" }, next: { opacity: 0, transform: "translateX(40px)" }, previous: { opacity: 0, transform: "translateX(-40px)" }, }; Previous: Cross-Component Context → · Next: Routing and Navigation →

entries.title: Bindings & Styles — ofa.js Docs
entries.description: The correct syntax for attr:, :prop, sync:, class:, :style, and boolean attributes.
headings: Interpolation does not work in attribute values
entries.text:
Template Bindings & Styles Property binding is the easiest part of ofa.js templates to mix up: knowing when to use : , when to use attr: , and when to use sync: determines whether the page updates correctly. Start with a table Syntax Direction Best for Boolean attributes :prop Data → property Plain values, objects, arrays Not suitable sync:prop Two-way Scalars such as strings, numbers, and booleans Possible, but attr: is preferred attr:name Data → HTML attribute href/title/data-*, boolean attributes Required class:name Data → class name States such as active/done/disabled — :style.prop Data → inline style Dynamic styles such as colors and sizes — One-way binding
: only writes data into the property; user interaction never writes back to the data. Objects and arrays passed to components through :prop are not serialized into strings. Two-way binding Form controls usually use sync: . Do not use it to bind objects or arrays : v5 explicitly forbids two-way syncing of objects to avoid reference confusion. Also avoid binding sync: to properties declared in attrs , since string serialization can cause circular updates. attr: HTML attributes and booleans Detail
attr: serializes the value into a string; but a false value removes the attribute entirely, while true sets an empty value. That is exactly what boolean attributes need. Don't use :disabled="false" . It renders disabled="false" , so the attribute still exists and the button stays disabled. Always write boolean attributes as attr:disabled="loading" . Class names
  • {{item.text}}
    • class:name adds the class when its condition is truthy and removes it when falsy. One element can have several. Intrinsic data attributes (type, status, level) are better expressed with attr: plus attribute selectors:
    .message[type="sent"] { color: #2563eb; } .message[type="failed"] { color: #dc2626; } Inline styles

    Style property names use camelCase ( fontSize , borderRadius ). Values must be valid CSS strings; add units yourself when needed. data() in stylesheets Besides inline styles, you can read data inside data() can also appear in @media conditions and in This approach only applies to a component's own styles; for cross-component theming use CSS variables or match-var. entries.description: ofa.js component structure, attrs/data, prop passing, slots, custom events, and component reuse.
entries.text:
Core concepts Components A component is a reusable Web Component module. It has its own Shadow DOM, reactive data, external attrs, and an interface for emitting events outward. Module Contract Field Required Description tag Yes Component tag name; it must match at usage attrs No Scalar attributes passed in from outside, reflected to HTML attributes data No Internal reactive state; put objects and arrays directly here proto No Methods, getters/setters watch No Watch changes to data/attrs ready/attached/loaded/detached No Lifecycle hooks When tag is not declared, the framework infers the tag name from the filename: user-card.html → . Declaring it explicitly is still recommended so that renaming or moving the file doesn't silently change the component's public tag. attrs and data attrs are the component's public inputs, suitable for strings, numbers, and booleans; data is the component's internal state, suitable for arrays and objects. Their keys must not overlap: export default { tag: "user-card", attrs: { userId: 0, compact: false, }, data: { profile: null, loading: false, }, }; When passed from outside, kebab-case names map to camelCase fields automatically: Pass dynamic values with a : prefix; use attr: for boolean attributes: Importing Components At the top of a page template, use to import a component file asynchronously. It returns immediately and does not block the page's first render: When you need to ensure a component is registered before use, await load() in the module function: export default async ({ load }) => { await load("./user-card.html"); return { data: {} }; }; Slots
Default title

Alice

This is default slot content

 The default slot receives child nodes without a slot attribute; named slots match slot="name" , and a slot can contain fallback content. Custom Events this.emit("save", { data: { id: 1, name: "Alice" }, }); Events default to bubbles: true and composed: false . Set composed: true explicitly when an event needs to escape the Shadow DOM; this is especially common when pages nest o-page . A component's PATH points to the URL of its registration file; relative resources in the component template, such as img src and style url() , resolve against PATH rather than against the URL of the page that uses it. entries.title: Cross-Component Context — ofa.js Docs
entries.description: o-provider, o-consumer, o-root-provider, getProvider, and dispatch.
entries.text:
Data Cross-Component Context o-provider places data into a subtree, and o-consumer consumes it from the nearest provider. This suits passing user info, themes, and business context across several component layers, avoiding prop drilling. Providers and consumers

{{userId}} / {{userName}}

The consumer walks up the DOM to find the nearest provider with the same name. The provider must be an ancestor of the consumer; a sibling will not be found. Runtime updates A provider's HTML attributes are read only once, during initialization. To update at runtime you must change its data properties directly; setAttribute does not work: // Correct: change the provider's data const provider = $("#userProvider"); provider.userName = "Bob"; // Wrong: setAttribute does not broadcast to consumers provider.ele.setAttribute("user-name", "Bob"); Nesting and reconnection When several providers with the same name are nested, their data is merged field by field, and the provider closer to the consumer overrides fields from the farther one. A consumer's name can also be changed dynamically; after the change it looks up the nearest provider with the new name again. Defaults: o-root-provider When no provider with the same name exists, the consumer falls back to the document-level root-provider. When both exist, the provider closer to the consumer wins. Looking up a provider explicitly const provider = this.getProvider("userInfo"); provider.userName = "Carol"; // consumers update automatically // any element can look up a provider $(".profile").getProvider("userInfo"); // global root provider const root = $.getRootProvider("theme"); Providers dispatching events to consumers $("#chatProvider").dispatch("new-message", { data: { text: "Hello" }, }); When not to use it Passing values only between parent and child: use :prop / sync: ; Sharing business state across pages: use $.stanz() ; Contexts that are purely styling, such as theme colors or sizes: prefer CSS variables or match-var . entries.title: Data & Watchers — ofa.js Docs
entries.description: Reactive data, computed getters, watch listeners, and common edge cases.
headings: data is an object, not a function
entries.text: Data Data and Watchers data is the reactive state of a component or page. It is powered by stanz, so deep changes to objects and arrays automatically trigger view updates. data is an object, not a function export default async () => ({ data: { count: 0, user: { name: "Alice", tags: [] }, todos: [], }, }); Each component instance has its own data. Assigning to nested objects and array push / splice / sort all trigger updates: this.user.name = "Bob"; this.user.tags.push("admin"); this.todos.splice(index, 1); this.todos = this.todos.filter((item) => !item.done); Computed properties Use getters in proto ; do not use Vue-style computed: data: { count: 0, firstName: "", lastName: "" }, proto: { get double() { return this.count * 2; }, get fullName() { return `${this.firstName} ${this.lastName}`; }, set fullName(value) { [this.firstName, this.lastName] = value.split(" "); }, }, Use them in templates like ordinary fields: {{double}} , {{fullName}} . Getters are evaluated as soon as the template initializes, before ready. They only suit simple computations that depend on synchronous initial values. Do not put computations that depend on async data in a getter; use a data field and assign it in the async callback instead, otherwise a TypeError may occur and break rendering for the whole page. Watchers data: { count: 0, width: 0, height: 0, area: 0, }, watch: { count(value, { watchers }) { if (!watchers) return; // first call during initialization console.log("count changed to", value); }, "width,height"() { this.area = this.width * this.height; }, user() { // objects and arrays are watched deeply console.log("user changed"); }, }, The second callback argument is { watchers } , the set of changes merged during the current debounce cycle. watchers[0] carries name , oldValue , value , type , target , and args . A watch function runs once when component initialization completes; at that point watchers is empty, and the call is used to establish the watch. If you do not need business logic to run during initialization, check if (!watchers) return; first. Avoiding write-back loops // Wrong: watch count and also change count in the callback watch: { count(value) { this.count = value + 1; }, }, When you need a derived value, use a computed property, or add an explicit trigger condition. Do not unconditionally write back to the watched data inside a watch. watch and async data data: { userId: 0, profile: null }, watch: { async userId(id) { if (!id) return; this.profile = await fetchProfile(id); }, }, Watch callbacks can be async functions. With concurrent requests, track a request sequence number or use AbortController so an older request cannot overwrite a newer result. Previous: Conditionals and Lists → · Next: Global State →

entries.description: Things to know when deploying an ofa.js app to any static server, CDN, or subdirectory.
headings: Loading the framework from a CDN
entries.text: Reference Deployment ofa.js apps have no build step, so deployment is essentially putting the source directory on any static server. There is no Node.js runtime dependency and no bundler. Minimal deployment Upload the entry HTML, page modules, components, and assets in their original directory structure: site/ ├── index.html ├── app-config.js ├── pages/ │ ├── home.html │ └── detail.html ├── components/ │ └── user-card.html └── assets/ The static server only needs to return correct MIME types. Pay particular attention to: Extension Content-Type .html text/html; charset=utf-8 .mjs text/javascript; charset=utf-8 .js text/javascript; charset=utf-8 .css text/css; charset=utf-8 .json application/json; charset=utf-8 Loading the framework from a CDN <script type="module" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ofajs/ofa.js@refs/heads/v5/dist/ofa.min.mjs" ></script> You can also download the dist file into your own static directory to avoid depending on a third-party CDN. When using router / scsr, remember to deploy them too and keep ofa.js loading first. Deploying in a subdirectory All asset paths support relative paths. When the app lives at https://example.com/app/ , ./detail.html in a page module resolves to /app/detail.html with no base path configuration. Avoid hardcoding absolute paths that start with / in your code. Caching strategy do not cache the HTML entry, or cache it briefly, so a new version is picked up after release; .mjs / .js files can use hashed filenames for long-term caching; disable caching during development so pages do not keep loading old modules after edits (see Common pitfalls ). o-router and scsr o-router uses hash URLs and needs no server rewrite at deployment: <o-router fix-body> <o-app src="./app-config.js"></o-app> </o-router> scsr requires every URL to return the corresponding HTML. For static deployment, each path needs a real file; for server deployment, output HTML generated from a template per path. Do not fall back every path to the same empty shell, or first-screen content is lost. CORS and local files Page modules load via fetch and components load as module scripts, so both must go over HTTP. Opening an HTML file directly ( file:// ) is blocked by the browser's CORS policy. For local preview, use any static server: $ npx serve . # or $ python3 -m http.server 3000 Previous: Full examples → · Back to: Docs overview →

entries.description: on:, one:, $event, two-way form binding, custom events, and event bubbling.
entries.text:
Template Events & Forms Bind events with on: and one-time events with one: . Form control values stay in two-way sync with data through sync: . Binding methods A bare identifier ( save ) is resolved as a proto method and automatically bound to this . Complex expressions run directly. String literals inside expressions must be quoted, otherwise they are treated as variable names. Event object $event is the native event object. Data from custom events lives in event.data , while the original DOM event fields remain available. One-time events
Click to unbind
one: unbinds automatically after the first trigger, which suits initialization, dismissing notices, and similar cases. Two-way form binding sync: is only for scalars. A form object can live in data as a whole, but each field binding must still target a specific scalar. Submitting a form
Custom events A component or page emits an event on its own: this.emit("save", { data: { id: 1, name: "John Doe" }, bubbles: true, // true by default composed: true, // set when the event must cross the Shadow DOM boundary }); Consumers listen for it and read event.data : When an o-page embedded in the host's Shadow DOM emits an event upward, bubbles: true and composed: true must both be present, otherwise the host never receives it. Naming suggestions Use lowercase kebab-case for event names: data-changed , form-save ; Reuse native event names such as click , input , and submit ; Don't prefix event names with on ; the template's on: already expresses that. entries.title: Lifecycle — ofa.js Docs
entries.description: Timing, order, and resource cleanup for ready, attached, loaded, and detached.
entries.text: Core concepts Lifecycle Components and pages share the same set of lifecycle hooks. Understanding the order they run in keeps you from touching elements before the DOM exists and helps you clean up timers and listeners properly. The four hooks Hook When it runs Typical uses ready() Template rendered and DOM created, though not necessarily in the document yet Initialize the DOM and third-party libraries, measure the initial state attached() The element is mounted into the DOM Start timers, add global listeners, load shared state loaded() The element, its child components, and async resources have all finished loading Finalization that depends on the full component tree, hiding loading indicators detached() The element is removed from the DOM Clear timers, listeners, and shared-state references On first mount the order is ready → attached → loaded ; detached is called when the element is removed. A complete cleanup example export default { tag: "clock-view", data: { now: Date.now(), }, attached() { this._timer = setInterval(() => { this.now = Date.now(); }, 1000); this._onResize = () => { this.width = window.innerWidth; }; window.addEventListener("resize", this._onResize); }, detached() { clearInterval(this._timer); window.removeEventListener("resize", this._onResize); }, }; Timers, global event listeners, and shared-state references should all be released in detached ; otherwise updates may still fire after the component is destroyed, leaking memory. ready vs. attached ready is the right place to work with a component's own Shadow DOM, for example querying this.shadow.$("#id") . If the logic depends on the element's actual size or position in the document, attached is safer. ready() { this.shadow.$("#canvas").css.width = "100%"; }, attached() { const rect = this.ele.getBoundingClientRect(); this.width = rect.width; }, Async data and computed properties Getters in proto are evaluated as soon as the template initializes, before ready . They are only suitable for simple computations over synchronous initial values: data: { count: 0 }, proto: { get double() { return this.count * 2; }, }, If a computation depends on an async API, don't put it in a getter. Use a data field instead and assign it in the async callback: data: { user: null, roleText: "" }, proto: { async loadUser() { const user = await fetchUser(); this.user = user; this.roleText = user.role === "admin" ? "Admin" : "User"; }, }, ready() { this.loadUser(); }, For more debugging scenarios, see Common Pitfalls . Previous: Pages → · Next: Template Directives →

entries.title: Nested Routing — ofa.js Docs
entries.description: Multi-level nested routing with shared layouts via export const parent and slots.
entries.text: Application Nested routing When several pages share the same navigation and sidebar, put the common structure in a parent page and mount child pages under the parent's through export const parent . Parent page: the layout Child page: declare parent parent resolves relative to the child page's own address. The child page is responsible only for the content inside slot ; the shared header/footer and sidebar stay in the parent. Behavior when switching When child pages under the same parent switch, the parent is not destroyed — only the slot content is replaced; the parent's data, scroll position, and loaded components are preserved; entering or leaving a child page through the parent fires the parent's routerChange ; a parent can declare parent too, forming multiple levels of nesting. The structure this site uses This site itself is an instance of the pattern: docs/origin/cn/layout.html ← site layout (nav, footer, docs sidebar) docs/origin/cn/index.html ← home page, mounted on the layout docs/origin/cn/docs/*.html ← docs pages, mounted on the same layout Every docs page ends with: export const parent = "../layout.html"; As a result, switching docs articles does not rebuild the header/footer or the left-hand table of contents — only the body area updates. Common pitfalls Forgetting in the parent, so the child page's content does not show; a wrong parent path, which loads the page standalone and drops the layout; putting routerChange on the child page — it only fires on the parent; using reserved names such as back , goto , or src in the parent's data, which makes registration fail. When you visit ./detail.html?id=42&tab=info , query.id is "42" . entries.description: Troubleshooting ReferenceError, reserved-name conflicts, boolean attributes, o-page src, and caching issues.
headings: ReferenceError: the template references an undeclared key
TypeError: a getter depends on data that has not arrived yet
SyntaxError: a bare literal in a directive value
Changes not taking effect: check the cache first
entries.text: Reference Common Pitfalls and Troubleshooting Pages that don't render, render only halfway, or ignore code changes — most problems trace back to a handful of fixed causes. Match the error message first, then check the template expressions. ReferenceError: the template references an undeclared key Every expression in a template is evaluated during initialization, so any key it references must first be declared in data or attrs . An undeclared key throws immediately and aborts rendering of the whole page: Error evaluating element expression: ':value="flag"' Caused by: ReferenceError: flag is not defined Fix: add the field to data with a safe default, for example data: { flag: false } . TypeError: a getter depends on data that has not arrived yet Computed property getters run as soon as the template initializes, before ready . If a getter reaches into a deep field of asynchronous data, it may throw a TypeError and crash the whole page. // Wrong: user is still an empty object get roleText() { return ROLE_TEXT[this.user.role]; } Switch to a data field and assign it in the async callback: data: { user: null, roleText: "" }, proto: { async loadUser() { const user = await fetchUser(); this.user = user; this.roleText = ROLE_TEXT[user.role] || ""; }, }, ready() { this.loadUser(); }, SyntaxError: a bare literal in a directive value The values of attr: , :prop , sync: , and class: are all parsed as JavaScript expressions: Referencing $host from a top-level o-if may fail silently; referencing $host from a top-level attr: may not error but never set anything. At the root level, always use data fields and proto methods. Use attr: for boolean attributes No {{ }} inside attribute values Link Link o-page src is immutable Keep the o-page mounted and pass parameters through child page methods; when you need a rebuild, wrap it in o-if so it is destroyed and recreated. Hash routing format // Wrong location.origin + location.pathname + "#./pages/set.html" // Right location.origin + "/#/pages/set.html" Changes not taking effect: check the cache first ofa.js caches loaded page modules, and the static server may cache HTML as well. If hash navigation still shows old content after you edit a file and the console reports no errors: Make the dev server disable HTTP caching (e.g. http-server -c-1 ); Do a full-page refresh with a complete URL carrying a new query; In automated tests, load the whole page with page.goto(url) instead of relying on hash navigation. Wrapper objects and .ele // Wrong $("o-app").current.shadowRoot // Right $("o-app").current.ele.shadowRoot.querySelector(".item") $("o-app").current.src Previous: Plugins and Extensions → · Next: Complete Examples →

entries.text:
Reference Plugins and Extensions Plugins are optional capabilities that only take effect when referenced; they are not part of the default ofa.js build. They attach to the global $ already loaded by the page and never pull in a second framework instance. Available plugins Plugin Capability Usage formdata Two-way binding between container form values and stanz objects $("#form").formData() inject-host Hoists style/link tags from the shadow to the host, reaching deep through slots body-ghost Teleports template content to the end of body for rendering (dialogs / overlays) global-link Injects a global stylesheet into components mounted after it Importing Import the source form directly, or use the classic script or ESM dist form: // monorepo / npm source import "ofa.js/packages/plugins/formdata/formdata.mjs"; // dist classic script (with dist ofa.js) // dist ESM import ".../packages/plugins/formdata/dist/formdata.min.mjs"; Plugins must load after ofa.js because they attach to the global $ ; if it is missing they throw immediately. formData
const data = $("#profile").formData(); data.username; // read data.username = "Yao"; // write back to the form data.revoke(); // release the binding Checkboxes are aggregated into an array, and multi-select, radio, and file inputs each have their own handling. A custom form component only needs to expose a value property and set name to participate. inject-host ::slotted() can only reach the first level of slotted content. To style elements deep inside a slot, use to hoist the styles to the host: Write the full component path in selectors to avoid leaking styles into other components; use this sparingly in cases that update styles frequently. body-ghost When dialogs, toasts, or overlays need to escape a parent's overflow or transform constraints, teleport the content to body:
Framework bindings follow the element as it moves, and native events bubble from its real DOM position. global-link The stylesheet is injected only into the shadow of components mounted after it; once o-global-link is removed, new components no longer receive the styles. It leaks into global scope, so use it carefully. match-var (core style query) To switch a component's internal styles based on CSS variables, use the core ; it requires no extra plugin: Conditions come from the values of CSS variables. On the outside, use data() to write data into the variables: Firefox: if styles do not switch immediately after a variable changes, call $.checkMatch() manually to trigger a re-check. entries.title: Routing & Navigation — ofa.js Docs
entries.description: goto/replace/back, olink, query parameters, o-router hash routing, and router-change.
entries.text: Application Routing and navigation ofa.js pages navigate in one of two modes: hash routing (o-router), which switches only inside the front-end app, and scsr, where every URL is a real document. The page navigation API is the same in both modes. Page navigation API // Inside a page module, `this` is the page instance this.goto("./detail.html?id=42"); // push onto the page stack this.replace("./detail.html"); // replace the current page without adding history this.back(); // go back this.forward(); // requires allowForward: true in the app config For declarative navigation, use olink : View details olink only takes effect inside o-app . It goes through in-app routing and transition animations without reloading the whole page. Do not add olink to external links. Passing parameters via query this.goto("./detail.html?id=42&tab=info"); export default async ({ query }) => ({ data: { id: query.id, tab: query.tab || "info", }, }); query is an argument of the page module function, not this.$route . To react to query changes, read it in the page module function; changing the address of the same page reloads the module. o-router: hash routing router is a bridge package and must be loaded after ofa.js; fix-body makes html/body full size; removing it reverts the change; the page stack is synced to the hash, for example #/pages/detail.html?id=42 ; refresh, deep links, sharing, and forward/back all restore the page without server rewrites; a page works with only one o-app. Hash URL format // Correct location.origin + "/#/pages/detail.html?id=42" // Wrong: an extra pathname or ./ location.origin + location.pathname + "#./pages/detail.html?id=42" Watching routing changes this.app.on("router-change", (event) => { const { name, src } = event.data; console.log(name, src); }); name is goto , replace , back , or forward ; src is the target page address. The routerChange hook in a page module fires only on the parent layout page, where it is used to highlight the current article. When you need real paths Hash routing suits pure front-end apps. If every URL must be crawlable, directly accessible, and shareable, use scsr real-path routing . The page API, nested layouts, and animation behavior are identical in both. Previous: o-app app → · Next: Nested routing →

entries.title: Global State — ofa.js Docs
entries.description: Use $.stanz() to create reactive state shared across pages, and mount and clean it up correctly.
entries.text: Data Global State When several pages or components need to share the same data, create reactive state with $.stanz() . It does not rely on global variables, and it does not persist automatically. Creating shared state // store.js export const cart = $.stanz({ items: [], total: 0, }); export const session = $.stanz({ user: null, theme: "dark", }); $.stanz() returns a deeply reactive proxy. Assigning to nested objects and array push / splice notifies every consumer. Using it in a page Mount/unmount convention: attach the shared state to your own data in attached , and clear the reference in detached , so the state does not keep referencing a destroyed component. Reading and writing shared state cart.items.push({ id: Date.now(), name: "ofa.js merchandise", count: 1, }); cart.total = cart.items.reduce( (sum, item) => sum + item.count, 0, ); When several pages read the same cart , a change made in any one of them propagates to the other pages and components. Watching state directly const tid = cart.watch(() => { console.log("cart changed", cart.total); }); // when it is no longer needed cart.unwatch(tid); watch watches deeply, so changes in child objects and arrays also fire. Inside components it is better to attach the state to data and let the template update automatically rather than manipulating the DOM by hand. Local state vs. shared state Scenario Approach Used only in the current component data Passing values between parent and child components :prop / sync: Business data across levels o-provider / o-consumer Cross-page, globally shared $.stanz() Pure styling themes CSS variables / match-var For a more structured way to share data across levels, see Cross-Component Context . Previous: Data and Watchers → · Next: Cross-Component Context →

entries.title: Template Directives Overview — ofa.js Docs
entries.description: Complete table of ofa.js template directives: interpolation, attributes, events, two-way binding, conditionals, and lists.
entries.text:
Template Template Directives Overview ofa.js template syntax lives directly in HTML: directives bind data, events, and rendering logic. There is no JSX and no template file that needs compiling. Directive reference Syntax Purpose Example {{expr}} Text interpolation, limited to element text content {{message}} :html Render HTML content
:prop One-way property binding sync:prop Two-way property binding attr:name HTML attribute binding class:name Conditional class name
  • :style.prop Inline style binding

    on:event Event binding : is one-way binding and sync: is two-way. For true , attr: sets an empty attribute; for false , it removes the attribute. That is why boolean attributes must use it. Class names and styles

  • class: adds or removes a class based on a boolean expression; :style.prop uses camelCase property names. For the full rules, see Bindings & Styles . Events A bare method name is automatically bound to this , and you can also write expressions directly. Data from custom events is read through event.data . See Events & Forms . Conditions and lists

    Greater than 10

    Greater than 5

    5 or less
    • {{$data.text}}
    Conditional tags must be written consecutively; inside o-fill only $data , $index , $host , $parent , and $ele are available. See Conditions & Lists . Where data comes from Every variable used in a template must first be declared in data or attrs . An undeclared variable is not undefined : it throws a ReferenceError and aborts rendering of the whole page. export default async () => ({ data: { name: "ofa.js", count: 0, inputValue: "", loading: false, todos: [], }, proto: { get doubleCount() { return this.count * 2; }, async save() { this.loading = true; await submit(); this.loading = false; }, }, }); Previous: Lifecycle → · Next: Bindings & Styles →

entries.title: 01 · Your First Page — ofa.js Tutorial
entries.description: A page in ofa.js is just an HTML file: structure, styles, and logic all live in one file.
headings: Change one line, run it once
The three things you just wrote
entries.text: Tutorial · 01 Your first page A page in ofa.js is just an HTML file: structure, styles, and logic all live in one file. A page module is declared with <template page> . Write the content you want to show in the template, put the data in data , then use {{ }} to place data into text. Change one line, run it once Change name in the editor to your own name, then press Ctrl + S ( ⌘ + S on Mac) or click "Run code" and watch the preview on the right update. The three things you just wrote <template page> : declares that this is a page module; data : the page's reactive data; change it and the page updates; {{name}} : inserts a value from data into the text. Common pitfall: the <script> must be written inside <template page> ; every field used in the template must first be declared in data , otherwise the whole page throws a ReferenceError . Try it yourself Add a city field to data and display it on the page with {{city}} . Next: 02 · Data and interpolation →

entries.title: 10 · Computed Properties & Watchers — ofa.js Tutorial
entries.description: proto getters compute synchronously; watch observes changes and handles side effects.
headings: How getters and watch divide the work
entries.text: Tutorial · 10 Computed Properties and Watching Getters in proto compute synchronously; watch observes changes and handles side effects. For values derived from existing data, use a getter in proto . When you need to do extra work after data changes (logging, writing to external storage), use watch . How getters and watch divide the work get total() : use it in templates like a normal field; it updates automatically with its dependencies; watch.qty(value, { watchers }) : runs after the data changes; watch is called once during initialization, when watchers does not exist yet, so you can use if (!watchers) return to skip that first call. Limits of getters: a getter is evaluated when the template initializes, so it can only depend on synchronous data that already exists. If you depend on async data returned by an API, store the result in a data field first, then assign it in the async callback. Try it yourself Add a "discount" input (0–1) so the total price is calculated with the discount; then use watch to log discount changes. Previous: 09 · Editing a List → · Next: 11 · Lifecycle →

entries.title: 11 · Lifecycle — ofa.js Tutorial
entries.description: ready → attached → loaded, then detached on removal; clean up timers and listeners in detached.
entries.text: Tutorial · 11 Lifecycle ready → attached → loaded, then detached on removal; clean up timers and listeners in detached. Pages and components share a fixed set of lifecycle hooks. The most commonly used are ready (the DOM is created), attached (mounted to the page), and detached (removed). Timing and responsibilities ready : the template has rendered and you can query the DOM; attached : the element has entered the document; a good place to start timers and add global listeners; loaded : the element itself and its async resources have finished loading; a good place to remove a loading state; detached : the element has left the document; you must clean up timers, listeners, and references to shared state. What happens without cleanup: timers keep running and keep mutating data after the page is gone, and listeners hold on to references from the old page, causing memory leaks. This is the most common lifecycle mistake. Try it yourself Change the timer to update every 0.5 seconds and to stop adding seconds while paused (the example already does this). Then try resetting seconds to zero in detached and watch what happens when you navigate away and come back. Previous: 10 · Computed Properties and Watching → · Next: 12 · Your First Component →

entries.title: 12 · Your First Component — ofa.js Tutorial
entries.description: Split reusable UI into <template component> and load it with l-m.
entries.text: Tutorial · 12 Your First Component Split reusable UI into <template component> and load it with l-m. Pages organize content; components own a reusable piece of UI. A component is also an HTML file, but its root node is <template component> and it declares a unique tag . Two files, two tabs The tabs at the top of the editor switch between page.html and hello-card.html . The page loads the component with <l-m src="./hello-card.html"> , and after that you can use <hello-card> like a normal HTML tag. tag : the component's tag name; it must match the name used where it is called; a component's data is isolated, so each of the two cards keeps its own count; a component's <style> only applies to that component. The file name is not the tag name: the tag name comes from the tag declared in the component, and is inferred from the file name only when it is missing. Don't rely on inference — declare it explicitly. Try it yourself Change the heading and button text in the component, then add a third card to the page and check whether the three cards count independently. Previous: 11 · Lifecycle → · Next: 13 · Component Parameters →

entries.title: 13 · Component Parameters — ofa.js Tutorial
entries.description: Pass external data into a component via attrs; keep internal state in data.
entries.text: Tutorial · 13 Component Parameters External data reaches the component through attrs; the component keeps its own state in data. Attributes a component receives from outside are declared in attrs with default values; state that changes inside the component lives in data . The two must not share names. attrs vs data attrs : scalar values passed in from outside (name, role, starting level); they are reflected to HTML attributes; data : the component's own reactive state; outside code does not modify it directly; in the example, startLevel is a string, and the component converts it to a number with Number() . Don't modify attrs directly: a child component treats attrs as read-only input. If you need derived state, copy it into data . That keeps the source of the data clear and prevents parent and child from overwriting each other. Try it yourself Add a level data field and an input to the page, then pass it to the second component dynamically with attr:start-level="level" . Previous: 12 · Your First Component → · Next: 14 · Slots and Events →

entries.title: 14 · Slots & Events — ofa.js Tutorial
entries.description: slots let a component receive external content; emit tells the outside world what happened inside.
entries.text: Tutorial · 14 Slots and Events slot lets a component receive outside content; emit reports what happens inside the component to the outside. Use <slot> when the component should keep its structure but let the consumer decide the content. When something happens inside the component — a click, a save — notify the consumer with this.emit() . Slots <slot> : the default slot, which receives the content inside the component tag; <slot name="hint"> : a named slot; the consumer marks content with slot="hint" ; content inside the slot tag is the default fallback content. Custom events Inside the component, call this.emit("confirm", { data: {...} }) , and have the page listen with on:confirm="onConfirm" ; the event payload is in event.data . If the event must cross multiple levels of Shadow DOM, also add bubbles: true, composed: true . One-way data flow: a component does not modify the page's data directly; it only reports what happened and lets the page decide how to handle it. That is what lets the same component be reused on different pages. Try it yourself Add a "Cancel" button to the component that emits a cancel event; have the page listen for it and change the hint text to "Cancelled". Previous: 13 · Component Parameters → · Next: 15 · Cross-level Context →

entries.title: 15 · Cross-Level Context — ofa.js Tutorial
entries.description: Share data across a component subtree with o-provider / o-consumer.
headings: How to choose vs. global state
entries.text: Tutorial · 15 Cross-Level Context Once the component hierarchy gets deep, passing attrs down level by level is tedious; use o-provider and o-consumer to put data into a subtree so descendants can consume it by name from the nearest ancestor. So far, data has been passed from parent to child components with attrs . If one piece of data has to cross many component layers, forwarding it level by level becomes exhausting. o-provider attaches data to an ancestor, and an o-consumer at any depth below can read it directly. Three cards The first two cards are inside the o-provider and read the provider's Yao / maintainer; The third card is outside the provider, so it falls back to the default user of o-root-provider ; The component's o-consumer uses watch:user-name="name" to sync the context property into its own data. Three easy pitfalls: A provider's HTML attribute is read only once at initialization; to update at runtime, change its data property directly ( provider.userName = ... in the example) — setAttribute does not broadcast. The provider must be an ancestor of the consumer; neither siblings nor outer levels can find it. Declare default values in data for any fields the consumer syncs, otherwise initialization throws a ReferenceError . How to choose vs. global state Use provider / consumer for data shared by only one component subtree; use $.stanz from the next lesson for state shared across pages and the whole app. For style context such as theme colors and sizes, prefer CSS variables or match-var . Try it yourself Add a user-department field to the provider and show the department in the cards; then add a button to the provider that switches the user for the whole subtree. Previous: 14 · Slots and Events → · Next: 16 · Global State →

entries.title: 16 · Global State — ofa.js Tutorial
entries.description: When several components share state, create a module-level store with $.stanz and mount/clean it up in attached/detached.
entries.text: Tutorial · 16 Global State When several components share the same state, create a module-level store with $.stanz and mount it in attached, then clean it up in detached. A component's own data belongs only to itself. When multiple components need to read and write the same data, create a reactive store with $.stanz() and share it from a separate module. Three files store.mjs : exports only $.stanz({ count: 0 }) ; counter-panel.html : both component instances reference the same store; page.html : hosts two panels plus the increment and decrement buttons. In attached , each component sets this.sharedState = store directly, and in detached it clears the reference with this.sharedState = {} . The template reads sharedState.label and sharedState.count directly; when the store changes, both panels update automatically. Convention: declare a placeholder sharedState: {} in data first, then mount the store in the attached phase and clear it in the detached phase. Only then can you avoid memory leaks and stale references held after the component is destroyed. How to choose: if the data belongs to one component subtree rather than the whole app, the previous lesson's o-provider / o-consumer fits better; see Cross-Level Context . Try it yourself Add step to the store so the "+1" button adds store.step each time; then add a button that sets step to 5. Previous: 15 · Cross-Level Context → · Next: 17 · Pages and Routing →

entries.title: 17 · Pages & Routing — ofa.js Tutorial
entries.description: o-app manages the page stack: switch pages with olink / goto, pass query parameters, and go back with back.
entries.text: Tutorial · 17 Pages and Routing o-app manages the page stack: navigate with olink / goto, pass parameters with query, and return with back. A multi-page app uses <o-app src="./app.mjs"> as its container. app.mjs holds only app configuration, such as the home page address and transition animation. Three files app.mjs : home points to the home page, pageAnime configures the transition animation; home.html : navigates to the about page with olink or goto() ; about.html : reads parameters from query and returns with back() . olink is declarative navigation and does not reload the page; this.goto(url) navigates from code. query arrives as an argument to the page module function, not on this . o-app only accepts app configuration: do not pass a page module directly to o-app src . For a single page use o-page src ; for a multi-page app use o-app plus the page address. Try it yourself Add an "About page (with parameters)" button to the home page that navigates with goto("./about.html?from=home-btn") ; then show the source on the about page. Previous: 16 · Global State → · Next: 18 · Nested Layouts →

entries.title: 18 · Nested Layouts — ofa.js Tutorial
entries.description: Child pages declare a parent, and the parent uses a slot to host them; the parent survives child page switches.
entries.text: Tutorial · 18 Nested Layouts Child pages declare parent, and the parent page receives them through a slot; switching child pages does not destroy the parent. Put shared structure such as navigation bars and sidebars in the parent page; child pages contain only their content and attach under the parent's <slot> via parent . How the layout works layout.html : navigation + <main><slot></slot></main> ; home.html / settings.html : export const parent = "./layout.html" ; The parent's routerChange fires when child pages switch, and is used to update the active navigation highlight. When the two child pages switch back and forth, the parent instance is not recreated; navigation state and layout are preserved. Don't duplicate the layout in child pages: write navigation and the footer once, in the parent; child pages only care about their own content. For multi-level nesting, the parent can declare a parent too. Try it yourself Add another child page, profile.html , plus a matching nav item, and confirm the layout doesn't flicker when switching. Previous: 17 · Pages and Routing → · Next: 19 · Async and Loading States →

entries.title: 19 · Async & Loading States — ofa.js Tutorial
entries.description: Drive the UI with loading / error / success states for async requests, and never put async results in getters.
entries.text: Tutorial · 19 Async and Loading States Drive the UI with the three async states loading / error / success; don't put async results in a getter. Page initialization often has to wait for an API. Don't wrap async logic in a getter; use explicit state fields instead: loading , error , and user , and let them drive the UI. Recommended flow Start the request: status = "loading" , clear the previous error; On success: write the result into data, status = "done" ; On failure: write the error message into error , status = "error" . The UI uses o-if / o-else-if / o-else to show loading, error, and content respectively. Why explicit state matters: a single user cannot distinguish "not started yet", "loading", and "failed to load". State fields give each case a definite UI, and make interactions such as disabling buttons or retrying easy to add. Try it yourself Give the request a 600ms delay (the example already has one) and disable the "Reload" button while loading; then try making the failure message clickable to retry. Previous: 18 · Nested Layouts → · Next: 20 · Putting It Together: A Todo List →

entries.title: 02 · Data & Interpolation — ofa.js Tutorial
entries.description: data can hold strings, numbers, booleans, objects, and arrays; {{ }} also supports simple expressions.
entries.text: Tutorial · 02 Data and interpolation data can hold strings, numbers, booleans, objects, and arrays, and {{ }} can evaluate simple expressions. data is a plain object, but ofa.js turns it into reactive data. Inside the template, {{ }} can do more than read fields: it can evaluate expressions and reach nested properties. Rules {{user.name}} : access a nested field of an object; {{user.age + 1}} : the contents of {{ }} are JavaScript expressions; :html="note" : renders a string as HTML; use it only for trusted content. Remember: {{ }} works only in an element's text content. For attribute values use attr: / :prop from the next lesson; writing <a href="{{url}}"> has no effect. Try it yourself Add a city field to user and display it as "City: xxx"; then try changing note to plain text and observe the difference between :html and {{ }} . Previous: 01 · Your first page → · Next: 03 · Dynamic attributes →

entries.title: 20 · Putting It Together: Todo List — ofa.js Tutorial
entries.description: Combine lists, forms, conditionals, computed properties, watchers, and localStorage into a complete app.
entries.text: Tutorial · 20 Putting It Together: A Todo List Wire lists, forms, conditionals, computed properties, watchers, and localStorage into one complete app. The final lesson combines the earlier capabilities: add todos from an input, check and delete list items, filter by status, and have the data saved automatically in the browser. What this lesson uses sync:value / sync:checked : form and list-item editing; o-fill + fill-key : list rendering and reuse; get visibleItems() / get remaining() : filtering and counts; watch.items : writes to localStorage when the data changes. Try refreshing the preview on the right: the todos are restored, because watch wrote them to browser storage when the data changed. Next steps: split the todos into components (lessons 12–14), share them across pages with $.stanz (lesson 16), and wrap it all in a layout (lesson 18) — that's a complete app. Try it yourself Add a "Clear completed" button; then add an edit button to each todo that switches the text row into an input. Previous: 19 · Async and Loading States →

entries.title: 03 · Dynamic Attributes — ofa.js Tutorial
entries.description: Use attr: for HTML attributes and :prop for DOM properties; boolean attributes must use attr:.
entries.text: Tutorial · 03 Dynamic attributes Use attr: for HTML attributes and :prop for DOM properties; boolean attributes must use attr:. Attributes in a template come in two kinds: attr: binds an HTML attribute, :prop binds a DOM property on the element. Do not write dynamic values as href="{{url}}" . Why two kinds of syntax attr:href , attr:title : end up as HTML attributes; :value : sets the DOM value property, suited to form elements; attr:disabled="!ready" : use attr: for boolean attributes; when the condition is false the attribute is actually removed. Why boolean attributes cannot use :prop: :disabled="false" leaves disabled="false" behind, so the attribute still exists and the button stays disabled. The correct form is attr:disabled="false" . Try it yourself Change the initial value of ready to true and see that the button starts out enabled; then change it back and click the button to enable it. entries.title: 04 · Styles & Classes — ofa.js Tutorial
entries.description: <style> in a page only applies to that page; class: and :style let styles follow data changes.
entries.text: Tutorial · 04 Styles and class A page's <style> applies only to that page; class: and :style let styles follow data changes. A <style> in a page template is collected into the page's Shadow DOM and does not leak into other components. :host selects the page/component itself. Three common forms :host : styles the page container, for example display:block ; class:active="active" : adds the class when the condition is true and removes it when false; :style.background="..." : inline style; use camelCase for the property name. Choosing between them: use class: for structural states (selected, done) and :style for individual values such as color or size. Do not build long style strings inside the template. Try it yourself Add another class bound with class:highlight="active" , give it a background color in <style> , and watch what changes when you toggle the state. Previous: 03 · Dynamic attributes → · Next: 05 · Events →

entries.title: 05 · Events — ofa.js Tutorial
entries.description: Listen to events with on:; use expressions for simple logic and proto methods for complex logic.
entries.text: Tutorial · 05 Events Listen for events with the on: prefix: use an expression for simple logic and a proto method for anything more involved. Event bindings are always written as on:event-name . The value can be a single expression or the name of a method on proto ; methods are automatically bound to the current page instance. Two styles on:click="count++" : best for logic that fits on one line; on:click="decrement" : best for multi-step or reusable logic; on:input="onNameInput($event)" : pass $event when you need the native event object. Don't reach for the DOM: in a handler, just change this.count and the page updates automatically. You only need real DOM access for things like measuring size, focusing an element, or initializing a third-party library. Try it Add a limit to decrement : don't let the count go below 0. Then add a button that multiplies the count by 2. Previous: 04 · Styles and class → · Next: 06 · Two-way binding →

entries.title: 06 · Two-Way Binding — ofa.js Tutorial
entries.description: sync: keeps forms and data in two-way sync; it works best with scalar values.
entries.text: Tutorial · 06 Two-way binding sync: keeps a form field and data in sync in both directions. Best for scalar values. sync: does two things at once: it updates the form when data changes, and writes user input back into data. It works well for scalar values such as strings, numbers, and booleans. Common form fields sync:value="name" : text inputs, textarea, select; sync:checked="subscribe" : the checked state of a checkbox; The preview below updates as you type, which shows the value has been written back to data . Don't sync objects: two-way binding an object leads to confusing references. To edit an object or array, bind to a specific field with sync:value="$data.field" , or handle the input in an on:input method. Try it Add an "Age" number input ( type="number" ), bind it with sync:value , and show next year's age in the preview. Previous: 05 · Events → · Next: 07 · Conditional rendering →

entries.title: 07 · Conditional Rendering — ofa.js Tutorial
entries.description: o-if / o-else-if / o-else control whether content exists.
headings: The three tags must be consecutive
entries.text: Tutorial · 07 Conditional rendering o-if / o-else-if / o-else control whether content is present. To show different content based on state, use <o-if :value="condition"> . When the condition is false the content is removed; when it is true the content is created again. The three tags must be consecutive o-if must have a :value ; o-else-if tests the next condition; o-else takes no :value and acts as the final fallback. Use class for frequent toggling: if you are only switching a color or showing/hiding something, prefer class: so the DOM is kept; o-if destroys and recreates content, so it suits conditions that rarely change or cases where resources really need to be released. Try it Change scores below 60 to "Fail", and add an 80–89 "Good" tier. Previous: 06 · Two-way binding → · Next: 08 · List rendering →

entries.title: 08 · List Rendering — ofa.js Tutorial
entries.description: o-fill renders arrays; use $data, $index, and $host inside list items.
entries.text: Tutorial · 08 List rendering o-fill renders an array; inside each item, use $data, $index, and $host. Render an array in a loop with <o-fill :value="items"> . Inside an item you cannot write item.text directly; use the scope variables the framework provides, such as $data . Item scope $data : data for the current item, for example $data.text ; $index : the current index, starting at 0; $host : the page instance; call methods such as $host.removeItem(id) ; fill-key="id" : always add this when there is a unique field, so items can be reused when entries are added or removed. Why fill-key matters: without a key, deleting an item in the middle makes all the items after it get rebuilt; if an item contains an input or local state, that state is lost. Use id to tell the framework "this is still the same item." Going further: for nested lists, use $parent to access outer data; o-fill inside table rows or a <select> requires <template is="replace-temp"> , and complex structures can live in a named template. See Conditionals and lists for complete examples. Try it Add a "Done" button after each item that toggles the item's done state when clicked (first add a done field to the data). Previous: 07 · Conditional rendering → · Next: 09 · Editing a list →

entries.title: 09 · Editing Lists — ofa.js Tutorial
entries.description: push/splice on arrays update the view automatically; inline editing syncs directly to $data fields.
entries.text: Tutorial · 09 Editing a list push/splice on an array update the view automatically; inline editing syncs straight to $data fields. Arrays in ofa.js are reactive: in-place operations such as push and splice trigger updates, so there is no need to reassign the whole array. Inline editing Each item's input is bound to $data.name , so user input is written straight to the object in the array. Combined with fill-key="id" , this item won't be rebuilt when you reorder the list or delete other items. When to replace the array: when you get a completely new list from an API, this.items = newList is clearer; when adding, removing, or editing a few items on the page, use push / splice . Try it Add an "↑" button to each row that swaps it with the row above (hint: use items.splice($index - 1, 2, currentItem, previousItem) ).
